title: Expected Taylor polynomial error
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $m\in\mathbb N$, and let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ have finite $(m+1)$st absolute moment. Let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $(m+1)$ times continuously differentiable, and suppose $C\in\mathbb R$ satisfies $|\psi^{(m+1)}(t)|\le C$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. For all $a,b\in\mathbb R$, \[\left|\int_\Omega\psi(a+bX(\omega))\,d\mu(\omega)-\int_\Omega\sum_{j=0}^{m}\frac{\psi^{(j)}(a)}{j!}(bX(\omega))^j\,d\mu(\omega)\right|\le\frac{C}{(m+1)!}|b|^{m+1}\int_\Omega|X(\omega)|^{m+1}\,d\mu(\omega).\]
hypotheses_covered: $X$ has finite $(m+1)$st moment in the $L^{m+1}$ sense
